newsitem.title: ALBANIA: SOCCER-TIRANA CLUBS HOLD FIRST GAME SINCE UNREST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TIRANA CLUBS HOLD FIRST GAME SINCE UNREST.

text.p: Two leading Albanian soccer clubs will play a friendly match in Tirana on Saturday, the first game between top teams in two months and a symbol of the capital's gradual return from near-anarchy.
State-owned television said the Tirana soccer club was organising the match against the capital's other club Partizani on Saturday. Ticket receipts would be donated to an orphanage.

"A traditional match between two of the best-known clubs in soccer history -- Tirana and Partizani, will be held tomorrow with the great message of spiritual calm, charity and civic humanism," the television said.
The match coincides with an Albanian World Cup qualifier against Ukraine on Saturday, to be played on neutral ground in Grenada, Spain, because of armed unrest in the Balkan state.
Albania named a 20-man squad drawn exclusively from Albanians playing for foreign clubs for the group nine qualifiers with Ukraine and another against Germany on April 2.
Albania's first division national championship has been suspended since the end of January because of the armed turmoil sweeping the Balkan country after the collapse of pyramid savings schemes.
"It will not be held for the championship, there will be no winners no losers. The money gathered from the ticket selling will be donated to the orphanage in Tirana," the television said.
The game will be played in Tirana's stadium, across the city from the national soccer stadium which was used for evacuation of foreign nationals by helicopter earlier this month.
